proposition: Access and audience attention expanded faster than artist income and employment security.
mechanism: Connectivity and platform distribution lower release and discovery costs, while revenue and bargaining power remain concentrated.
primary_measures: Release counts; attention rates; music-income share; payment delay; contract status; career continuity.
supporting_evidence_needed: Platform histories plus artist income bands, contracts, payment records, and interviews.
falsification_or_revision_rule: Revise if median music-income share, timely payment, rights knowledge, and full-time continuity rise alongside attention across genres and regions.

proposition: Corporate sponsors filled functions that labels, public arts institutions, and live infrastructure did not reliably provide.
mechanism: Brands finance production, curation, distribution, and promotion in exchange for reputational and marketing value.
primary_measures: Funding source; ownership; selection route; production budget; artist compensation; post-campaign career outcomes.
supporting_evidence_needed: Programme credits, contracts, brand interviews, participant and rejected-applicant accounts, comparison releases.
falsification_or_revision_rule: Revise if non-brand labels, public funds, venues, and independent revenues provide comparable scale and continuity.
status_before_fieldwork: Strong case evidence; population effect unknown

proposition: Platforms democratized entry more than visibility.
mechanism: Uploading became easier, but recommendation, playlisting, marketing budgets, and existing networks shape discovery.
primary_measures: Release volume; playlist access; concentration of views/streams; marketing spend; network centrality; chart entry.
supporting_evidence_needed: Platform snapshots, artist analytics, campaign histories, playlist records, and negative cases.
falsification_or_revision_rule: Revise if attention concentration declines and comparable tracks without institutional support achieve similar discovery rates.

proposition: Regional identity gains national and global visibility most readily when paired with metropolitan production, visual packaging, or institutional sponsorship.
mechanism: Intermediaries translate regional forms into formats legible to brands, platforms, and cosmopolitan audiences.
primary_measures: Language; origin; producer location; funding; visual codes; credit prominence; ownership; follow-on income.
supporting_evidence_needed: Regional and metropolitan comparison cases, credit networks, interviews with artists and communities.
falsification_or_revision_rule: Revise if regionally based, self-controlled releases achieve durable reach and income without metropolitan or corporate mediation.

proposition: Diaspora and Indian audiences materially increase the scale of Pakistan's largest musical successes.
mechanism: Shared languages, diaspora networks, foreign media, and cross-border recommendation expand addressable audiences beyond Pakistan.
primary_measures: Audience geography; foreign chart entry; touring; collaborator location; media placement; diaspora support.
supporting_evidence_needed: Artist analytics, chart histories, tour data, diaspora interviews, and cross-border platform comparisons.
falsification_or_revision_rule: Revise if major successes are predominantly sustained by domestic listening and domestic revenues.

proposition: International awards and viral hits increase symbolic prestige more reliably than they strengthen domestic institutions.
mechanism: Recognition accrues to particular artists and transnational networks without automatically producing local rights, finance, venue, or training capacity.
primary_measures: Awards and global attention versus changes in contracts, collective management, studios, venues, labels, and employment.
supporting_evidence_needed: Institutional time series, spillover interviews, investment records, and pre/post career networks.
falsification_or_revision_rule: Revise if breakthroughs generate measurable, durable domestic investment and broad-based career improvements.

proposition: Visibility became more socially diverse, but conversion from visibility to livelihood remained unequal by class, gender, language, and geography.
mechanism: Digital entry can bypass some gatekeepers while equipment, mobility, safety, unpaid time, and professional networks remain unequally distributed.
primary_measures: Representation; income share; payment; ownership; safety incidents; travel access; family subsidy; professional role.
supporting_evidence_needed: Artist sample, purposive interviews, case comparisons, and representation-to-income conversion analysis.
falsification_or_revision_rule: Revise if underrepresented groups obtain comparable ownership, compensation, continuity, and decision power after matching for career stage.
